figure: Figure 22.1 (Attention vs projection prefill FLOP crossover), left panel
issue: The annotation 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K' marks an intersection that is not the crossover claimed in the caption and in Note 22.1-1 (PDF 380 / printed 360).
evidence: Legend defines exactly four curves: linear 2·N·L (red solid), quadratic 4·n_layers·L²·d (purple dashed, full-square), total (full-square) (orange dashed), total (causal-triangle) (green dotted). The causal-triangle quadratic term 2·n_layers·L²·d is never plotted. Recompute with the stated geometry (N=70e9, n_layers=80, d=8192): the green total = 2·N·L + 2·n_layers·L²·d lies strictly ABOVE the red linear curve for every L, so green never crosses red; the only intersection near 106.8K is green(total causal) × purple(full-square quad), since L + 0.5Q = Q exactly when Q = 2L, i.e. L = N/(n_layers·d) = 70e9/(80·8192) = 106,811 ≈ 106.8K. By contrast the full-square annotation 'full-square quad overtakes ~53.4K' correctly points at purple × red (Q = L at N/(2·n_layers·d) = 53,406). So the number 106.8K is right, but the drawn crossing is a different pair of curves than the one the caption describes ('the quadratic attention term overtakes the parameterized-linear term at ... ~106.8K under causal-triangle counting'). A reader checking the caption against the figure can infer the false claim that the green total curve crosses the linear curve at 106.8K, or that the marked green×purple intersection represents causal attention overtaking the linear term. (Intersection geometry inferred from the 150 dpi render; confirm arrow tip at high zoom.)
root_cause: The causal-triangle quadratic term has no curve of its own, so the annotation was attached to the nearest visible intersection at the correct x-value.
correction: Either (a) add the causal-triangle quadratic term 2·n_layers·L²·d as its own curve so it visibly crosses the red linear curve at ~106.8K (mirroring how purple × red shows the full-square case), or (b) keep four curves but relabel the annotation to state what is actually crossing (e.g. 'causal total = full-square quad at ~106.8K') and add a one-line note that the causal attention-term-vs-linear crossing is not plotted.
acceptance_test: At high zoom, the annotation's arrow tip resolves to a named pair of plotted curves, and that pair's intersection is the crossover the caption claims — or the caption/annotation explicitly says which crossing is and is not drawn.

issue: In-figure note 'hatched = live production stage (not gated): Serve' is ambiguous and can be read as 'entry into Serve is ungated', which contradicts the sixth gate.
evidence: Seven stages (Data→Train→Eval→Canary→Observe→Promote→Serve) with six gate boxes at the six seams, the last being 'Promote / cost ok / PASS' at the Promote→Serve seam; the red FAIL bar text confirms 'Gates check ... and promotion cost'. Caption: 'Six gates align with the transition seams: PASS permits the next stage.' Since every seam including Promote|Serve carries a gate, 'not gated' cannot mean 'no gate before Serve'; the intended meaning is 'no gate follows Serve' (Serve is terminal/live). Both readings are grammatically available, and the false one directly contradicts the caption.
root_cause: Elliptical parenthetical that does not say which side of Serve lacks a gate.
correction: Rewrite the note as 'hatched = live production stage (no gate follows it): Serve' or 'hatched = terminal live stage'.
acceptance_test: A first-time reader cannot reasonably conclude that the Promote→Serve transition is ungated; the note's referent (before vs. after Serve) is explicit.

issue: Title verb order 'probe, measure, harden, loop' does not match the drawn and captioned step order.
evidence: Drawn order: 1 Red Team → 2 Probes → 3 Exposure → 4 Guardrails → 5 Metrics → 6 Green Team (arrows 1→2→3, 3→4, 4→5→6, red feedback 6→1). Caption order: 'red team → probe → exposure → guardrails → metrics → green team'. The title places 'measure' (step 5, Metrics) before 'harden' (step 4, Guardrails), i.e. it reverses two adjacent steps; it also omits 'exposure'. A reader who takes the title as the cycle sequence gets the order wrong.
root_cause: Slogan compressed to four verbs without preserving sequence.
correction: Reorder/reword the title to match the cycle, e.g. 'probe, expose, harden, measure, loop' or 'probe, harden, measure, loop'.
acceptance_test: The title's verb sequence is a subsequence of the drawn 1→6 order (hardening precedes measuring).

figure: Figure 20.1 (Fleet capacity vs host count), in-plot annotation
issue: ASCII 'N >= 22' (and ASCII hyphen 'rps - not scheduling overhead') in the UNUSED-capacity annotation, where the book elsewhere typesets ≥ and dash punctuation (e.g. Fig 23.1 box 2 'p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s').
evidence: Annotation text in the pink region reads 'UNUSED capacity (N >= 22): insufficient offered demand; S capped at 40 rps - not scheduling overhead'. Caption for the same figure uses proper operators/prose ('above saturation C_eff − S ...'). Glyph identification made at 150 dpi; confirm at high zoom before editing.
root_cause: Raw ASCII operators in figure annotation source rather than math-mode glyphs.
correction: Replace with 'N ≥ 22' and an en dash (or colon) in the annotation source.
acceptance_test: High-zoom render of the annotation shows ≥ and typographic dash consistent with the caption and with Fig 23.1.
